tries.prompt:
A character model sheet for a narrated animated film, drawn in this art style: our own K1 paper-cut look made minimal, the house look, as the reference image shows it. Every figure and prop is a few flat cut-paper shapes. Every figure and prop has a thick warm dark-brown ink outline and a thin light inner edge just inside it, and is creased once by a single straight diagonal line at the light's angle, its far side a deeper hue of its own colour turned toward violet, never grey and never black. A head is ONE simple shape inside one single thick outline, and the light inner edge runs round that one outline. Garments are flat planes: no pockets, no buttons, no stitching, no seams, no cuffs, no fabric texture. Hands are plain round paper circles at the end of each arm in its sleeve, the sleeve running from the shoulder to the hand: never a hand floating free of the body, never a bare arm, no thumbs, no fingers. Faces are three marks only: two small dark ink oval eyes, short brows and a one-line mouth. One muted hue per piece. The light: a warm, soft key light from the upper left; a soft paper grain on every piece and every plane; a small soft violet contact shadow under each figure, never a darker brown; a muted, warm palette in which only the film's accents are loud. Keep it K1: no white sticker border round the figures, no felt or stitching style, no big glossy eyes, no realistic anatomy. The look is stylised, attractive, expressive and minimal.

Image 1 is the house look: take its paper, its line and its light from it; its hands float free beside the body, which no figure on this sheet does. Image 2 is the plain lead's model sheet: his build, his head on his body with no neck, his pale cool grey paper and lilac shade, his three-mark face; hold him to it, his height and width unchanged. Image 3 is the plain lead as he was kept: the figure every film's plain lead is.

The person is the plain lead, the parable's "a certain man", exactly as his model sheet draws him: a small figure, a round head sitting right on a trapezoid body with no neck, his head nearly as wide as his hem, two short rounded stub legs under the hem; no hair, no ears, no nose, no shoes. One pale cool grey paper with a faint lilac cast for his head, hands, robe and legs (lit side #dbd6dc, shade side turned lilac-violet #b5a9d0, never a darker grey). A face of three marks: two short arched brows, two small dark oval dot eyes and a one-line mouth. For the wedding feast he wears his festive dress, the one thing the story changes: a longer robe of his own grey paper reaching to his shins, a quiet muted blue-green sash (#5f8f88) tied at the waist, and arms in sleeves of the same grey paper to the wrist, each round grey hand at the end of its sleeve, no thumbs. No pattern, trim, pockets or seams. His height and his width are his model sheet's: the sheet does not make him taller or slimmer. What he carries, and only where a pose names it: a small plain baby's bottle with a pale teat and no markings; a plain plate.

Draw him six times in one row, evenly spaced across the sheet, standing at rest with both arms hanging in their sleeves at the sides, each hand at its sleeve's end, left to right: one, facing the viewer straight on; two, turned three-quarters toward the viewer's left; three, in full profile facing the viewer's left; four, seen from directly behind; five, in full profile facing the viewer's right; six, turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. In profile one eye shows; from behind no face shows, only the back of the hair or headcloth and the garment's back.

This is a model sheet for the animators, not a scene: a plain warm cream paper ground with a soft paper grain and no place behind, one thin flat ground line in a slightly deeper cream under every figure, and a small soft violet contact shadow under each one. Every figure on the sheet is the same person at the same size: the same height, the same head size, the same garment length and the same hand size, their soles on the one ground line. The person stands about three and a third heads tall. One thick warm dark-brown outline runs round the whole silhouette of each figure, and the head's outline is the one line inside it: none on the nose, the ear or the hairline, and the hair, the ear and the garments meet as flat colour, never as their own outlined pieces. The hair and the beard are one brown, yet never one shape: the hair is its own shape behind the head, the face and its beard one shape in front of it, and a narrow dark band, the deep shade of that brown, nearly as dark as the outline, runs between the beard and each lock of hair beside it, as the kept concepts paint it, so the beard never runs into the hair. The key light comes from the upper left on every figure, whichever way it faces, so its lit side is always on the left and its far side turns a deeper hue of its own colour toward violet, never grey and never black. Each turn is its own drawing, never a mirror of another. Each arm is in its sleeve to the wrist, and each hand is a plain round paper circle of the skin's colour at its sleeve's end: no thumb, no fingers. The sleeve runs from the shoulder to the hand wherever the hand is, hanging at rest along the side or raised with it; a hand never floats free beside the body. No skin shows below the neck except the hands: never a bare arm, a forearm or a bare shoulder. No lettering anywhere: no labels, no names, no numbers, no arrows, no text, no grid, no boxes or frames round the figures.

The light: a warm, soft key light from the upper left; a soft paper grain on every piece and every plane; a small soft violet contact shadow under each figure, never a darker brown; a muted, warm palette in which only the film's accents are loud. Keep it K1: no white sticker border round the figures, no felt or stitching style, no big glossy eyes, no realistic anatomy. The look is stylised, attractive, expressive and minimal.

Image 1 is the house look: take its paper, its line and its light from it; its hands float free beside the body, which no figure on this sheet does. Image 2 is the plain lead's model sheet: his build, his head on his body with no neck, his pale cool grey paper and lilac shade, his three-mark face; hold him to it, his height and width unchanged. Image 3 is the plain lead as he was kept: the figure every film's plain lead is.

The person is the plain lead, the parable's "a certain man", exactly as his model sheet draws him: a small figure, a round head sitting right on a trapezoid body with no neck, his head nearly as wide as his hem, two short rounded stub legs under the hem; no hair, no ears, no nose, no shoes. One pale cool grey paper with a faint lilac cast for his head, hands, robe and legs (lit side #dbd6dc, shade side turned lilac-violet #b5a9d0, never a darker grey). A face of three marks: two short arched brows, two small dark oval dot eyes and a one-line mouth. For the wedding feast he wears his festive dress, the one thing the story changes: a longer robe of his own grey paper reaching to his shins, a quiet muted blue-green sash (#5f8f88) tied at the waist, and arms in sleeves of the same grey paper to the wrist, each round grey hand at the end of its sleeve, no thumbs. No pattern, trim, pockets or seams. His height and his width are his model sheet's: the sheet does not make him taller or slimmer. What he carries, and only where a pose names it: a small plain baby's bottle with a pale teat and no markings; a plain plate.

Draw only his head and the top of his shoulders, six times in a row, evenly spaced, all the same size. One to three are turned three-quarters toward the viewer's left: one, level, hopeful, the brows raised; two, level, wincing, the eyes squeezed and the mouth a tight wavy line; three, tilted a little, thinking. Four to six face the viewer straight on: four, level, at rest; five, level, wincing; six, lifted a little, tasting, the eyes closed in delight, a wide soft smile.

This is a model sheet for the animators, not a scene: a plain warm cream paper ground with a soft paper grain and no place behind, and nothing under the heads. Every head on the sheet is the same person at the same size: the same head size and the same hair, each head with the top of its shoulders only. No hands, no arms and no skin show below the neck. One thick warm dark-brown outline runs round the whole silhouette of each figure, and the head's outline is the one line inside it: none on the nose, the ear or the hairline, and the hair, the ear and the garments meet as flat colour, never as their own outlined pieces. The hair and the beard are one brown, yet never one shape: the hair is its own shape behind the head, the face and its beard one shape in front of it, and a narrow dark band, the deep shade of that brown, nearly as dark as the outline, runs between the beard and each lock of hair beside it, as the kept concepts paint it, so the beard never runs into the hair. The key light comes from the upper left on every figure, whichever way it faces, so its lit side is always on the left and its far side turns a deeper hue of its own colour toward violet, never grey and never black. Each turn is its own drawing, never a mirror of another. No lettering anywhere: no labels, no names, no numbers, no arrows, no text, no grid, no boxes or frames round the figures.
